title_en: Bearing Witness That Muhammad Is the Messenger of God
body_ar:
الرسل حق، وأفضلهم خاتمهم محمد بن عبد الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، الذي اختاره الله من العرب وخصه على من قبله بخصائص وميزات، وجعل دينه خير الأديان، ولذلك ينبغي على المسلم أن يتعرف على جوانب من حياة هذا النبي ونسبه وميزاته وما يتعلق بذلك.
وجوب اتباع محمد صلى الله عليه و سلم على جميع الخلق:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين، وأصلي وأسلم على من بعث رحمة للعالمين وعلى آله وأصحابه، ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين. أما بعد: فيقول الشيخ حفظه الله: والرسل حق والنبي العربي خاتمهم أعلاهم في الرتب ......
التكذيب بمحمد تكذيب بجميع الرسل:
بعد أن ذكر الرسل عليهم الصلاة والسلام ووجوب الإيمان بهم على سبيل الإجمال، ذكر التعويل على شهادة أن محمداً رسول الله، وهي الشهادة الثانية من الشهادتين، وهما ركنا الاعتقاد: فالركن الأول: شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله، وكل ما سبق من التفصيلات داخل في هذه الشهادة...
body_en:
*[Site synopsis]* The messengers are true, and the most excellent of them is the last of them, Muhammad ibn Abd Allah, God bless him and grant him peace, whom God chose from among the Arabs and whom He singled out above those before him with distinguishing features and marks of distinction, and whose religion He made the best of religions. For this reason the Muslim ought to acquaint himself with aspects of this Prophet's life, his lineage, his marks of distinction and what relates to these.

## The obligation upon all creation to follow Muhammad, God bless him and grant him peace

In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Mercy-Giving. Praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds. I ask God's blessing and peace upon the one sent as a mercy to the worlds, and upon his family and his Companions, and upon all who have taken guidance from his guidance and followed his practice until the Day of Judgement. To proceed: the Sheikh, may God preserve him, says: *And the messengers are true; and the Arabian Prophet is the seal of them, the highest of them in rank.* ......

## To deny Muhammad is to deny all the messengers

After mentioning the messengers, upon them be blessing and peace, and the obligation to believe in them in summary form, he mentioned the reliance placed upon bearing witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of God. This is the second of the two testimonies, and the two are the two pillars of belief: the first pillar is bearing witness that there is no god but God, and everything of the particulars that has gone before falls within this testimony …

flags.context: the record breaks off and the full text sits behind a download
options: render with an excerpt banner and link the .doc
flags.note: Excerpt only, style guide section 9. It breaks off on an ellipsis just as the second testimony is introduced, and the claim announced by the second section heading — that denying Muhammad is denying all the messengers — is never argued. The complete text sits behind /medias/doc/L-35.doc. The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends and completes nothing. Must not be rendered as a whole lesson.

flags.arabic: الفقرة الافتتاحية مقابل ما بعد العنوان الفرعي
flags.context: the synopsis paragraph against the transcribed opening of the lesson
options: mark the synopsis as the site's own and the remainder as the Sheikh's words
present the whole record as the Sheikh's words
flags.note: The record has two authors. The first paragraph is a synopsis written by the site — it speaks about the lesson and its subject in the third person and does not begin with the opening formula. Everything from the section heading onward is transcribed speech in the Sheikh's own voice. The site must not present the synopsis as his words.

flags.context: the formula introducing each quoted line of the versified creed being commented on
options: read it as the author of the versified base text, distinct from the lecturer
read it as Sheikh al-Dedew quoting his own verse
flags.note: Getting this referent wrong would misattribute a creedal formulation, so it is flagged on every record in which the formula appears. These lessons are a commentary on a versified creed (nazm): the transcriber introduces each base-text line with 'the Sheikh, may God preserve him, said', and the commentary follows. 'حفظه الله' is used of the living, which at first sight fits Sheikh al-Dedew himself. Three passages inside the run settle it otherwise. Record 719 has the speaker giving thanks for 'completing the commentary on the Sheikh's versification' and describing what 'the Sheikh' chose to leave undetailed — a commentator does not ordinarily speak of his own base text that way while expounding it. Record 716 describes the base text as a versification of the Mukhtaṣar of Khalil ibn Ishaq by 'one of the scholars'. Record 718 introduces the same quoted lines with 'the versifier said'. The reading adopted throughout this slice is therefore that 'the Sheikh' is the living author of the versified base text and the lecturer is his commentator. The author is nowhere named, and the identification should be confirmed by the Sheikh's office before publication, because the bracketed verse and the prose around it carry different attributions.

flags.context: the six dots standing where the commentary on the quoted verse should be
options: reproduce the source's own ellipsis and supply nothing
treat the gap as a transcription loss and note it
flags.note: A second break inside the record, of the same kind found in records 709 and 712 of this run. The commentary on the quoted line is missing entirely: the verse is given, six dots follow, and the text resumes under a new heading with 'After mentioning the messengers … he mentioned', which refers back to material the reader has not been shown. This makes the surviving paragraph read as a non-sequitur. The dots are the source's own and are reproduced; nothing has been supplied.

flags.arabic: وجوب اتباع محمد صلى الله عليه و سلم على جميع الخلق
options: The obligation upon all creation to follow Muhammad
That following Muhammad is obligatory for all created beings
flags.note: A heading stating a ruling of universal scope, which an English reader will meet before any argument for it — because the argument is precisely what the six dots have removed. 'وجوب' attaches to an act and is therefore the legal ruling, rendered 'obligation' per the fixed mapping. Note that the heading is the site's, that the served text never states it in the Sheikh's own voice, and that a claim of this kind read in English out of context bears on relations with non-Muslims; style guide sections 10 and 12 both apply. Note also the stray space in 'عليه و سلم' in the source, left as served.

flags.arabic: ذكر التعويل على شهادة أن محمداً رسول الله
options: he mentioned the reliance placed upon bearing witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of God
he mentioned dependence upon the testimony that Muhammad is God's Messenger
he turned to what rests upon the second testimony
flags.note: 'التعويل على' is to rest one's weight on something, to make it the thing depended upon. The referent of 'ذكر' — the subject who 'mentioned' — is the author of the versified base text, not the lecturer, on the reading settled in record 719; but this is a third-person verb with no expressed subject and the English keeps it as bare as the Arabic.

flags.context: the two testimonies described in the surviving paragraph
options: and the two are the two pillars of belief
and they are the two supports of the creed
flags.note: 'ركن' is fixed in the glossary as 'essential element', whose omission invalidates, as against a condition (sharṭ). 'Pillar' has been used here rather than 'essential element' because the phrase names the two testimonies of the creed, where 'pillar' is the settled English and the technical contrast with sharṭ is not in play. The same word is rendered 'pillar' in 'pillars of faith' throughout this run.

translator_notes: One of a run of fifteen records, IDs 707-721, in the written-creed section, all uploaded on 9 and 10 May 2011 within a few hours of one another, all built to the same template and all excerpts. Each carries a site-written synopsis, then a section heading, then the opening formula and the first lines of a lesson, and then breaks off on an ellipsis; the full text sits behind a .doc download in the /medias/doc/L-* series, numbered L-26 to L-39 in the same order as the IDs. The uniform timestamps are a bulk upload and say nothing about when the lesson was delivered.

The record contains two distinct voices and the English keeps them apart. The opening paragraph is a synopsis written by the site, about the lesson and in the third person; everything from the section heading onward is the Sheikh's own words as transcribed. Nothing in the synopsis may be quoted as his.

The source's final line, 'تحميل المادة' ('download the material'), is the label of a download link in the page furniture, not part of the text. It is recorded as source_download_link and omitted from body_ar and body_en.

The base text being commented on is identified inside this run. Record 719 has the Sheikh speaking of 'completing the commentary on the Sheikh's versification', and of that versifier's rendering of Khalil's Jāmiʿ in some five hundred lines; record 716 describes the base text as a versification of the Mukhtaṣar of Khalil ibn Ishaq whose opening section is on creed; and record 718 introduces the same quoted lines with 'the versifier said'. Taken together these settle that 'the Sheikh, may God preserve him' in this run is the living author of the versified base text and not the lecturer. The author is never named.
The record is broken twice, and what survives between the two breaks is a single paragraph that refers backward to text the reader cannot see. Of the two section headings, neither subject is reached.
The quoted line of verse is the same one quoted in record 708 of this run, there in square brackets and here without them. Reproduced as served in each case.
